cemc-galois-2007-01a.title: Compare the two sums
cemc-galois-2007-01a.body:
Both combinations contain one Cherry. Swapping the Apple for a Banana raises the total from 62 to 66 cents, so a Banana costs $66 - 62 = 4$ cents more than an Apple.

**Answer: 4 cents; the Banana has the higher price.**

cemc-galois-2007-01a.title: Subtract equations
cemc-galois-2007-01a.body:
Let the prices (in cents) be $A$, $B$, $C$. Then $A + C = 62$ and $B + C = 66$. Subtracting, $B - A = 4$.

**Answer: 4 cents; the Banana has the higher price.**

cemc-galois-2007-01b.title: Mango and Pear cost the same
cemc-galois-2007-01b.body:
Let the prices be $M$, $N$, $P$ cents. From $M + N = 60$ and $P + N = 60$, we get $M = P$. Then $M + P = 68$ becomes $2P = 68$, so $P = 34$.

**Answer: 34 cents**

cemc-galois-2007-01b.title: Add all three
cemc-galois-2007-01b.body:
Adding the three equations: $2(M + N + P) = 188$, so $M + N + P = 94$. Since $M + N = 60$, $P = 94 - 60 = 34$.

**Answer: 34 cents**

cemc-galois-2007-01c.title: Find the Grapefruit first
cemc-galois-2007-01c.body:
Let the prices be $T$, $L$, $G$ cents: $T + L = 60$, $T - G = 6$, $G + T + L = 94$.

From the first and third, $G = 94 - 60 = 34$. Then $T = 34 + 6 = 40$ and $L = 60 - 40 = 20$.

**Answer: 20 cents**

cemc-galois-2007-01c.title: Eliminate T
cemc-galois-2007-01c.body:
From $T = G + 6$: the third equation becomes $2G + 6 + L = 94$, i.e. $2G + L = 88$, and the first becomes $G + 6 + L = 60$, i.e. $G + L = 54$. Subtracting, $G = 34$, so $L = 54 - 34 = 20$.

**Answer: 20 cents**

cemc-galois-2007-02a.title: Two radii plus an arc
cemc-galois-2007-02a.body:
The sector angle is $60^\circ$, which is $\frac{60}{360} = \frac16$ of a full circle. So the arc $AB$ has length $\frac16 \cdot 2\pi(12) = 4\pi$.

The perimeter is $OA + OB + \text{arc } AB = 12 + 12 + 4\pi = 24 + 4\pi \approx 36.6$.

**Answer: $24 + 4\pi$**

cemc-galois-2007-02a.title: Arc length formula
cemc-galois-2007-02a.body:
In radians, $60^\circ = \frac{\pi}{3}$, so the arc length is $r\theta = 12 \cdot \frac{\pi}{3} = 4\pi$. Perimeter: $24 + 4\pi$.

**Answer: $24 + 4\pi$**

cemc-galois-2007-02b.title: Two sixths of a circle
cemc-galois-2007-02b.body:
Each $60^\circ$ sector is $\frac16$ of a circle of radius 12, so has area $\frac16 \cdot 144\pi = 24\pi$.

Figure $ABCD$ is two such sectors: $2 \cdot 24\pi = 48\pi \approx 150.8$.

**Answer: $48\pi$**

cemc-galois-2007-02b.title: One third of a circle
cemc-galois-2007-02b.body:
The two sectors together have the same area as a single sector of angle $120^\circ$, which is $\frac13$ of a circle: $\frac13 \cdot 144\pi = 48\pi$.

**Answer: $48\pi$**

cemc-galois-2007-02c.title: 30-60-90 triangle
cemc-galois-2007-02c.body:
$OY$ is a radius, so $OY = 12$. Since $OA = OB$ and $\angle AOB = 60^\circ$, $\triangle OAB$ is equilateral, and $OX$ bisects $\angle AOB$, so $\angle AOX = 30^\circ$.

In the $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle $OAX$ with hypotenuse 12: $AX = 6$ and $OX = 6\sqrt3$.

So $XY = OY - OX = 12 - 6\sqrt3 \approx 1.61$.

**Answer: $12 - 6\sqrt3$**

cemc-galois-2007-02c.title: Pythagoras
cemc-galois-2007-02c.body:
$\triangle OAB$ is equilateral with side 12, and the perpendicular from $O$ bisects $AB$, so $AX = 6$. Then $OX = \sqrt{12^2 - 6^2} = \sqrt{108} = 6\sqrt3$, and $XY = 12 - 6\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $12 - 6\sqrt3$**

cemc-galois-2007-02d.title: Sector minus triangle, twice
cemc-galois-2007-02d.body:
By symmetry, $QS$ splits the shaded region into two equal parts. The right part is sector $PQS$ minus $\triangle PQS$.

- Sector $PQS$ has area $\frac16 \cdot 144\pi = 24\pi$.
- $\triangle PQS$ is equilateral with side 12 (as in part (c)); its height is $6\sqrt3$, so its area is $\frac12 \cdot 12 \cdot 6\sqrt3 = 36\sqrt3$.

So each part has area $24\pi - 36\sqrt3$, and the shaded region has area $48\pi - 72\sqrt3 \approx 26.1$.

**Answer: $48\pi - 72\sqrt3$**

cemc-galois-2007-02d.title: Inclusion–exclusion
cemc-galois-2007-02d.body:
The two sectors together make up the rhombus $PQRS$, with the shaded lens lying in both of them and every other point of the rhombus in exactly one. So area(sector $P$) + area(sector $R$) = area(rhombus $PQRS$) + area(shaded).

The rhombus is two equilateral triangles of side 12: area $2 \cdot 36\sqrt3 = 72\sqrt3$. So

$$\text{shaded} = 24\pi + 24\pi - 72\sqrt3 = 48\pi - 72\sqrt3.$$

**Answer: $48\pi - 72\sqrt3$**

cemc-galois-2007-03a.title: Edges and corners
cemc-galois-2007-03a.body:
A small cube has at least two painted faces exactly when it lies on an edge of the big cube (colours don't matter here).

- 8 corner cubes (three painted faces),
- each of the 12 edges has $5 - 2 = 3$ non-corner cubes (two painted faces).

Total: $8 + 12 \times 3 = 44$.

**Answer: 44**

cemc-galois-2007-03a.title: Subtract the rest
cemc-galois-2007-03a.body:
Of the $125$ small cubes, $3^3 = 27$ are inside (no paint), and each face has $3 \times 3 = 9$ cubes with exactly one painted face: $6 \times 9 = 54$. So $125 - 27 - 54 = 44$ cubes have at least two painted faces.

**Answer: 44**

cemc-galois-2007-03bi.title: Count along one edge
cemc-galois-2007-03bi.body:
A small cube with exactly two white faces lies on an edge but not at a corner (corner cubes have three faces, all white).

Along an edge there are $2k + 1$ cubes. Corners are white and the colours alternate along the edge, so the cubes in positions $1, 3, 5, \dots, 2k+1$ are white on both edge faces: that is $k + 1$ cubes, two of which are corners. (On an edge, the two visible squares of a cube have the same colour, since both are at the same position along the checkerboard pattern starting from a white corner.)

So each edge has $k + 1 - 2 = k - 1$ non-corner cubes with two white faces, and there are 12 edges:

$$12(k - 1) = 12k - 12.$$

Check with $k = 2$ (the 5-cube): each edge has positions 1–5, white at 1, 3, 5, so one non-corner cube per edge, 12 in total. ✓

**Answer: $12k - 12$**

cemc-galois-2007-03bii.title: Count, then solve
cemc-galois-2007-03bii.body:
Cubes with at least two white faces are those with exactly two white faces ($12k - 12$ of them, by part (i)) plus the 8 corner cubes (three white faces). Total: $12k - 4$.

If $12k - 4 = 2006$, then $12k = 2010$ and $k = 167.5$, which is not an integer. So no value of $k$ works. ∎

cemc-galois-2007-03bii.title: Divisibility
cemc-galois-2007-03bii.body: The total $12k - 4$ is always $\equiv 8 \pmod{12}$ (equivalently, it is a multiple of 4). But $2006 = 4 \cdot 501 + 2$ is not a multiple of 4. So the count can never be 2006. ∎

cemc-galois-2007-04a.title: Try each number of yellow rods
cemc-galois-2007-04a.body:
With $x$ yellow and $y$ green rods we need $5x + 3y = 62$, so $62 - 5x$ must be a non-negative multiple of 3. Checking $x = 0, 1, \dots, 12$:

| $x$ | $62 - 5x$ | $y$ |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 57 | 19 |
| 4 | 42 | 14 |
| 7 | 27 | 9 |
| 10 | 12 | 4 |

(all other $x$ give a value not divisible by 3).

**Answer: 4 sets**

cemc-galois-2007-04a.title: Step from one solution
cemc-galois-2007-04a.body:
One solution is $x = 1$, $y = 19$. Replacing 3 yellow rods (15 cm) by 5 green rods (15 cm), or vice versa, gives all others: $x = 1, 4, 7, 10$ (with $x = 13$ we'd need $65 > 62$). That is 4 sets.

**Answer: 4 sets**

cemc-galois-2007-04b.title: Look for a common factor
cemc-galois-2007-04b.body:
Green rods are 3 cm and red rods are 9 cm. With $a$ green and $b$ red rods the length is $3a + 9b = 3(a + 3b)$, always a multiple of 3. Since 62 is not a multiple of 3, green and red cannot make a 62 cm pole.

(Every other pair works: 19 green + 1 yellow, 16 green + 2 black, 11 yellow + 1 black, 7 yellow + 3 red, 5 black + 3 red.)

**Answer: green and red**

cemc-galois-2007-04c.title: Reduce, then group the terms
cemc-galois-2007-04c.body:
Use $81 + a$ green, $81 + b$ pink, $81 + c$ violet and $81 + d$ red rods ($a, b, c, d \ge 0$). Then

$$3a + 4b + 8c + 9d + 81(3 + 4 + 8 + 9) = 2007 \implies 3a + 4b + 8c + 9d = 63.$$

Write it as $3x + 4y = 63$ with $x = a + 3d$, $y = b + 2c$. The solutions are $(x, y) = (1, 15), (5, 12), (9, 9), (13, 6), (17, 3), (21, 0)$.

- $x = a + 3d$ has $\lfloor x/3 \rfloor + 1$ solutions: $1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8$ for $x = 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21$.
- $y = b + 2c$ has $\lfloor y/2 \rfloor + 1$ solutions: $8, 7, 5, 4, 2, 1$ for $y = 15, 12, 9, 6, 3, 0$.

Total: $1\cdot8 + 2\cdot7 + 4\cdot5 + 5\cdot4 + 6\cdot2 + 8\cdot1 = 8 + 14 + 20 + 20 + 12 + 8 = 82$.

**Answer: 82**

cemc-galois-2007-04c.title: Fix the violet and red extras
